captions.detailed: This 3D model is a rectangular pill organizer tray containing a grid of 21 open compartments arranged in 7 rows and 3 columns. The walls of each compartment are thin, uniform, and intersect to form a solid grid structure inside the outer frame. Small cylindrical nubs project from the outer ends of the frame, likely serving as hinge or latch points for an optional lid.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric grid-based pill organizer tray in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to configure the number of days (rows) and doses per day (columns), adjust the dimensions of each individual compartment, and optionally include small cylindrical latch nubs at the ends of the organizer.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using two box modules: 'box' (an end compartment with four closed walls) and 'box2' (an intermediate compartment with one open side to merge with the next). These are built using a difference of two cubes to create hollow, thin-walled structures. Nested for-loops arrange these boxes in rows and columns based on 'number_days' and 'number_per_day'. If 'nubs' is enabled, two cylinders are rotated, extruded, and translated to opposite outer ends of the tray.
